p0.original: Welcome to Principles of Economics 3e (Third Edition), an OpenStax resource. This textbook was written to increase student access to high-quality learning materials, maintaining highest standards of academic rigor at little to no cost.
p0.zh: 欢迎使用经济学原理 3e(第三版),一个OpenStax资源. 这本教科书的编写是为了增加学生获得高质量学习材料的机会,保持最高的学术严谨标准,费用低到免费.

p2.original: OpenStax is part of Rice University, which is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit charitable corporation. Our mission is to make an amazing education accessible for all. Through our partnerships with philanthropic organizations and our alliance with other educational resource companies, we’re breaking down the most common barriers to learning. Because we believe that everyone should and can have access to knowledge.
p2.zh: OpenStax是赖斯大学的一部分,该大学是一家501(c)(3)非营利慈善公司. 我们的使命是使所有人获得令人惊奇的教育。透过我们与慈善组织的合作, 以及我们与其他教育资源公司的联盟,因为我们相信,每个人都应该而且能够获得知识。

p5.original: Principles of Economics 3e is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 (CC BY-NC-SA) license, which means that you can non-commercially distribute, remix, and build upon the content, as long as you provide attribution to OpenStax and its content contributors, and distribute all derivatives under the same license.
p5.zh: "经济学原理3e"根据创用CC BY-NC-SA许可(CC BY-NC-SA)许可,获得许可,这意味着你可以在内容上进行非商业发行,再混合,并在此基础上发展,只要您为OpenStax及其内容贡献者提供归属,并在同一许可下分配所有衍生物.

p6.original: Because our books are openly licensed, you are free to use the entire book or select only the sections that are most relevant to the needs of your course. Feel free to remix the content by assigning your students certain chapters and sections in your syllabus, in the order that you prefer. You can even provide a direct link in your syllabus to the sections in the web view of your book.
p6.zh: 因为我们的书是公开的许可, 你可以自由使用全书, 或者只选择与你课程的需要最相关的部分。 请随意,按照您喜欢的顺序,通过为您的学生分配教学大纲中的某些章节来重新组合内容。 您甚至可以在您的课程大纲中提供直接链接到您书的网页视图中的章节。

p7.original: Instructors also have the option of creating a customized version of their OpenStax book. Visit the Instructor Resources section of your book page on OpenStax.org for more information.
p7.zh: 教官们还可以选择创建其OpenStax书的定制版本. 请访问OpenStatus.org上的教学资源栏目了解更多信息。

p9.original: In Principles of Economics 3e, most art contains attribution to its title, creator or rights holder, host platform, and license within the caption. For any art that is openly licensed, non-commercial users or organizations may reuse the art as long as they provide the same attribution to its original source. (Commercial entities should contact OpenStax to discuss reuse rights and permissions.) To maximize readability and content flow, some art does not include attribution in the text. If you reuse art from this text that does not have attribution provided, use the following attribution: Copyright Rice University, OpenStax, under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 license.
p9.zh: 在《经济学原则3e》中,大多数艺术都包含对其所有权、创作者或权利持有人、主机平台的归属以及标题中的许可。 对于任何公开许可的艺术品,非商业用户或组织只要为原始来源提供同样的归属,即可重新使用该艺术品。(商业实体应联系OpenStax,讨论再使用权和权限. )为了最大限度地提高可读性和内容流,一些艺术没有在文本中包括归属. 若您重新使用未提供归属的文本中的艺术,请使用以下属性: 版权稻业大学 OpenStax, 依据 CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 许可.

p11.original: All OpenStax textbooks undergo a rigorous review process. However, like any professional-grade textbook, errors sometimes occur. In addition, economic data and related developments change frequently, and portions of the textbook may become out of date. Since our books are web based, we can make updates periodically when deemed pedagogically necessary. If you have a correction to suggest, submit it through the link on your book page on OpenStax.org. Subject matter experts review all errata suggestions. OpenStax is committed to remaining transparent about all updates, so you will also find a list of past and pending errata changes on your book page on OpenStax.org.
p11.zh: 所有OpenStax教科书都经过严格的审查程序. 然而,与任何专业级的教科书一样,错误有时也会发生. 此外,经济数据和相关发展变化频繁,教科书的部分内容可能过时。 由于我们的书籍以网络为基础,我们可以在认为教学上有必要时定期进行更新。 如果您有修改建议,请通过OpenStatus.org上的书页链接提交。专题专家审查所有错误建议。OpenStax 致力于保持所有更新的透明度,因此您也会在 OpenStax.org 的书页上找到一份过去和待发错误的更改列表.

p13.original: You can access this textbook for free in web view or PDF through OpenStax.org, and for a low cost in print.
p13.zh: 您可以通过OpenStax.org免费访问此教科书或PDF,并且可以低价打印。

p15.original: Principles of Economics 3e aligns to the topics and objectives of most introductory economics courses. Arranged in the traditional progression from microeconomics to macroeconomics, it allows flexibility in coverage and sequencing. The text uses conversational language and ample illustrations to explore economic theories, and provides a wide array of examples using both fictional and real-world scenarios. The third edition has been carefully and thoroughly updated to reflect current data and understanding, as well as to provide a deeper background in diverse contributors and their impacts on economic thought and analysis.
p15.zh: 经济学原则3e与大多数入门经济学课程的主题和目标相一致。 它在从微观经济学向宏观经济学的传统发展过程中安排,在覆盖面和顺序方面可以灵活。文本使用对话语言和丰富的插图来探索经济理论,并提供了大量使用虚构和现实世界情景的例子. 第三版经过认真和彻底的更新,以反映当前的数据和了解,并为各种贡献者提供更深入的背景及其对经济思想和分析的影响。

p17.original: In response to faculty feedback and to ease transition to a new edition, Principles of Economics 3e retains the organization of the previous editions. The book covers the breadth of economics topics and also provides the necessary depth to ensure the course is manageable for instructors and students alike. We strove to balance theory and application, as well as the amount of calculation and mathematical examples.
p17.zh: 作为对教职员反馈的回应,为方便向新版的过渡,"经济学原理3e"保留了前几版的编排. 该书涵盖经济学专题的广度,并提供了必要的深度,以确保课程对教员和学生都是可以管理的。 我们努力平衡理论和应用,以及计算和数学实例的数量。

p18.original: The book is organized into eight main parts:
p18.zh: 该书主要分为八个部分:

p19.original: What is Economics?  The first two chapters introduce students to the study of economics with a focus on making choices in a world of scarce resources.
p19.zh: 什么是经济学? 前两章向学生介绍经济学的研究,重点是在资源稀缺的世界中作出选择.

p20.original: Supply and Demand, Chapters 3 and 4, introduces and explains the first analytical model in economics: supply, demand, and equilibrium, before showing applications in the markets for labor and finance.
p20.zh: 《供应与需求》,第3和4章,介绍并解释了经济学的第一个分析模式:供应、需求和平衡,然后展示在劳务和金融市场上的应用。

p21.original: The Fundamentals of Microeconomic Theory, Chapters 5 through 10, begins the microeconomics portion of the text, presenting the theories of consumer behavior, production and costs, and the different models of market structure, including some simple game theory.
p21.zh: "微观经济理论的基本原理"第5章至第10章开始文字的微观经济部分,介绍了消费者行为,生产和成本的理论,以及市场结构的不同模型,包括一些简单的游戏理论.

p22.original: Microeconomic Policy Issues, Chapters 11 through 18, covers the range of topics in applied micro, framed around the concepts of public goods and positive and negative externalities.  Students explore competition and antitrust policies, environmental problems, poverty, income inequality, and other labor market issues. The text also covers information, risk and financial markets, as well as public economy.
p22.zh: 《微观经济政策问题》第11章至第18章涵盖各种应用的微观专题,围绕公益物和积极及消极的外部效应的概念。学生探索竞争和反托拉斯政策,环境问题,贫困,收入不平等,以及其他劳动力市场问题.案文还涵盖信息、风险和金融市场以及公共经济。

p23.original: The Macroeconomic Perspective and Goals, Chapters 19 through 23, introduces a number of key concepts in macro: economic growth, unemployment and inflation, and international trade and capital flows.
p23.zh: 《宏观经济展望和目标》,第19至23章,在宏观方面提出了若干关键概念:经济增长、失业和通货膨胀、国际贸易和资本流动。

p24.original: A Framework for Macroeconomic Analysis, Chapters 24 through 26, introduces the principal analytic model in macro, namely the aggregate demand/aggregate supply model.  The model is then applied to the Keynesian and Neoclassical perspectives.  The expenditure-output model is fully explained in a stand-alone appendix.
p24.zh: 《宏观经济分析框架》第24至26章介绍了宏观中的主要分析模型,即总需求/总供应模型。 该模型随后被应用于凯恩斯主义和新古典主义视角.独立附录充分解释了支出-产出模式。

p25.original: Monetary and Fiscal Policy, Chapters 27 through 31, explains the role of money and the banking system, as well as monetary policy and financial regulation.  Then the discussion switches to government deficits and fiscal policy.
p25.zh: 《货币和财政政策》第27至31章解释了货币和银行系统的作用以及货币政策和金融监管。 然后,讨论转向政府赤字和财政政策。

p26.original: International Economics, Chapters 32 through 34, the final part of the text, introduces the international dimensions of economics, including international trade and protectionism.
p26.zh: 《国际经济》,第32至34章,案文的最后一部分,介绍了经济的国际层面,包括国际贸易和保护主义。

p28.original: The revision process incorporated extensive feedback from faculty who have used the book in their courses. They advised that the third edition changes focus on currency updates, integration of newer perspectives and more diverse contributors, and relevance to students’ lives and careers.
p28.zh: 修订过程吸收了在课程中使用该书的教职员工的广泛反馈。 他们建议,第三版的修改侧重于货币更新、新观点的融合和更加多样化的贡献者,以及与学生生活和职业的相关性。

p29.original: Current data and analysis: The authors have updated dozens of explanations, graphs, and tables containing financial, demographic, employment, and related economic data. The corresponding discussions provide context and interpretations of the data, including descriptions of change over time, cause-and-effect relationships, and balanced analysis of policies and opinions.
p29.zh: 现有数据和分析:作者更新了数十种解释、图表和表格,其中载有财务、人口、就业和相关经济数据。相应的讨论对数据提供了背景和解释,包括描述随时间演变的变化、因果关系,以及对政策和意见的平衡分析。

p30.original: Diverse perspectives and contributors: The third edition highlights the research and views of a broader group of economists. These include people from across the spectrum of economic thought, with a particular focus on those who take what are often considered non-traditional views of economic policy and government action. Examples include:
p30.zh: 不同观点和贡献者:第三版重点介绍了更广泛的经济学家群体的研究和观点。这些人包括来自经济思想各界的人,特别侧重于那些对经济政策和政府行动采取通常被认为是非传统观点的人。实例包括:

p31.original: Chapter 1: Esther Duflo, Abhijit Banerjee, and Michael Kremer regarding experimental analysis in development economics.
p31.zh: 第1章:Esther Duflo、Abhijit Banerjee和Michael Kremer关于发展经济学的实验分析。

p32.original: Chapter 4: Walter Williams and Thomas Sowell regarding the downsides of minimum wages.
p32.zh: 第4章:沃尔特·威廉姆斯和托马斯·索韦尔关于最低工资的下限.

p33.original: Chapter 13: Carlota Perez regarding employment shifts resulting from innovation; Mariana Mazzucato regarding government involvement in innovation; Elinor Ostrom and the “non-tragedy of the commons.”
p33.zh: 第13章:卡洛塔·佩雷斯关于创新带来的就业变化;马里安娜·马祖卡托关于政府参与创新;埃利诺·奥斯特罗姆和“公社无怨”。

p34.original: Chapter 14: William A. Darity Jr. on employment discrimination and market forces; Phyllis Ann Wallace and the EEOC.
p34.zh: 第14章:威廉·A.Darity Jr.,关于就业歧视和市场力量;Phyllis Ann Wallace和EEOC。

p35.original: Chapter 19: Kate Raworth regarding concepts for expanding economic measures beyond GDP and similar metrics.
p35.zh: 第19章:关于将经济措施扩大到国内生产总值和类似衡量标准以外的概念的凯特·拉沃思。

p36.original: Chapter 32: W. Arthur Lewis and the dual sector economy; Dambisa Moyo regarding the benefits and detriments of foreign aid.
p36.zh: 第32章:W节Arthur Lewis和双重部门经济;Dambisa Moyo关于外国援助的利弊。

p37.original: Relevance and engagement: In order to show the importance and application of economics in students’ lives and careers, the third edition directly addresses and expands topics likely to connect to various industries, issues, groups, and events. Brief references and deeply explored socio-political examples have been updated to showcase the critical—and sometimes unnoticed—ties between economic developments and topics relevant to students. Examples include education spending, the value of college degrees, discrimination, environmental policies, immigration policies, entrepreneurship and innovation, healthcare and insurance, and general financial literacy. Finally, the COVID-19 pandemic is referenced frequently to demonstrate its deep and evolving impacts on financial data, employment, and other aspects of the economy.
p37.zh: 相关性和参与性:为了显示经济学在学生生活和职业中的重要性和应用性,第三版直接讨论和扩展了可能与各种行业、问题、团体和事件相联系的主题。简短的参考资料和深入探讨的社会政治实例已经更新,以展示经济发展与学生相关议题之间的关键之处,有时是不被注意的。例子包括教育支出、大学学位的价值、歧视、环境政策、移民政策、创业和创新、保健和保险以及一般金融知识。 最后,经常提到COVID-19流行病,以表明其对金融数据、就业以及经济其他方面的深刻和不断变化的影响。

p38.original: FRED Data and Graphs: As in previous editions, the authors have included and referenced data from the Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED). In some cases, interactive FRED graphs are embedded directly in the web view of the book; students may magnify and focus on specific time periods, analyze individual data points, and otherwise manipulate the graphs from within the OpenStax reading experience. In others cases (and in the PDF), links to the direct source of the FRED data are provided, and students are encouraged to explore the information and the overall FRED resources more thoroughly. Note that other data sources, such as the Bureau of Labor Statistics, U.S. Census Bureau, and World Bank, usually include links in the captions or credits; instructors and students can also explore those sites for more detailed investigations of the topics at hand.
p38.zh: FRED数据和图表:与前几版一样,作者已经将联邦储备经济数据(FRED)的数据纳入并引用.在某些情况下,互动的FRED图形直接嵌入到书的网页视图中;学生可能会放大并专注于特定的时段,分析单个数据点,否则会从OpenStax阅读体验中操纵图形. 在另一些情况下(以及PDF中),提供了与FRED数据直接来源的链接,鼓励学生更彻底地探索这些信息和FRED总体资源.注意其他数据来源,如美国劳工统计局.人口普查局和世界银行通常在标题或学分中包括链接;教员和学生也可以探索这些网站,以便更详细地调查当前议题。

p40.original: Principles of Economics 3e includes updated and redesigned art to clarify concepts and provide opportunities for graphical interpretation. Many graphs are shown with accompanying data tables and explanations of the drivers and consequences of change.
p40.zh: 《经济学原则3e》包括更新和重新设计的艺术,以澄清概念并提供图形解释的机会。 许多图表都附有数据表和变化驱动因素及后果的说明。

p42.original: The narrative explanations and analysis presented in Principles of Economics 3e have been carefully crafted to provide a solid basis in economic concepts, flexibly approach skills and assess understanding, and deepen students’ engagement with the course materials. You will also find features that promote economic inquiry and explorations, including:
p42.zh: 《经济学原则3e》中提出的叙述性解释和分析经过精心设计,为经济概念、灵活处理技能和评估理解以及加深学生对教材的参与提供了坚实的基础。 您还可找到促进经济调查和探索的特征,包括:

p43.original: Bring It Home: These explorations include a brief case study, specific to each chapter, which connects the chapter’s main topic to the real word. It is broken up into two parts:  the first at the beginning of the chapter (in the intro module) and the second at chapter’s end, when students have learned what’s necessary to understand the case and “bring home” the chapter’s core concepts.
p43.zh: 带回家:这些探索包括一个简短的案例研究,每个章节都有具体的内容,将章节的主要话题与真实的词汇联系起来. 它被分为两部分:第一部分在章节的开头(在入门单元中),第二部分在章节的结尾,学生们已经了解到了解案情所必须的东西,以及章节的核心概念 " 带回家 " 。

p44.original: Work It Out: These worked examples progress through an analytical or computational problem, and guide students step by step to find out how its solution is derived.
p44.zh: Work It Out:这些工作实例通过分析或计算问题取得进展,并指导学生一步一步地找出解决方案的出处。

p45.original: Clear It Up: These boxes are deeper explanations of something in the main body of the text. Each Clear It Up starts with a question.  The rest of the feature explains the answer.
p45.zh: Clear It Up:这些框是文本正文中某些事物的更深层次的解释.每一个"清空起来"都从一个问题开始.其余特征解释解答.

p46.original: Questions for each level of learning

p47.original: Principles of Economics 3e offers flexibility in practice and assessment, and provides a range of opportunities to check understanding and encourage deeper thinking and application.
p47.zh: 《经济学原则3e》为实践和评估提供了灵活性,并为检查理解和鼓励更深入的思考和应用提供了一系列机会。

p48.original: Self-Checks are analytical self-assessment questions that appear at the end of each module. They “click to reveal” an answer in the web view so students can check their understanding before moving on to the next module. Self-Check questions are not simple look-up questions. They push the student to think beyond what is said in the text.  Self-Check questions are designed for formative (rather than summative) assessment. The questions and answers are explained so that students feel like they are being walked through the problem.
p48.zh: 自查是每个单元末出现的分析性自评问题。学生在进入下一个模块之前, 自查问题不是简单的查询问题。 他们逼学生思考 超越文本中所说的。 自查问题是为了形成性(而不是概括性)评估而设计的。 对问答进行解释,使学生感到他们正在经历问题。

p49.original: Review Questions are simple recall questions from the chapter in open-response format (not multiple choice or true/false). The answers can be looked up in the text.
p49.zh: 审查问题只是从章节中以公开答复形式(不是多重选择或真实/虚假)提出的简单召回问题。答案可以在文本中查看。

p50.original: Critical Thinking Questions are higher-level, conceptual questions that ask students to demonstrate their understanding by applying what they have learned in different contexts.
p50.zh: 批判性思考问题(Critical Thinking Questions)是更高层次,概念性的问题,要求学生通过应用他们在不同背景下学到的知识来展示他们的理解.

p51.original: Problems are exercises that give students additional practice working with the analytic and computational concepts in the module.
p51.zh: 问题在于使学生有更多实践与模块中的分析和计算概念合作。

p52.original: OpenStax is retiring Principles of Microeconomics and Principles of Macroeconomics for AP textbooks because they are outdated. We recommend that Advanced Placement instructors and students use the college-level textbooks.
p52.zh: OpenStax正在为AP教科书退休微观经济学原理和宏观经济学原理,因为其已经过时. 我们建议高级安置教员和学生使用大学一级的教科书。

p55.original:
David Shapiro, Pennsylvania State University
  David Shapiro is Professor Emeritus of Economics, Demography, and Women’s, Gender, and Sexuality Studies at the Pennsylvania State University.  He received a BA in economics and political science from the University of Michigan, and an MA as well as a PhD in economics from Princeton University.  He began his academic career at Ohio State University in 1971, and moved to Penn State in 1980. His early research focused on women and youth in the United States labor market. Following a 1978–79 stint as a Fulbright professor at the University of Kinshasa in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, his research shifted focus to fertility in Kinshasa and more broadly, in sub-Saharan Africa.  He has also received the top prize for teaching at both Ohio State and Penn State.
p55.zh: 宾夕法尼亚州立大学的David Shapiro是宾夕法尼亚州立大学经济学,人口学,以及妇女,性别,性和性学研究的荣誉教授.他曾获得密歇根大学经济学和政治学学士学位,普林斯顿大学经济学硕士和博士学位。1971年他在俄亥俄州立大学开始学术生涯,1980年移居宾州. 他的早期研究重点是美国劳动力市场上的妇女和青年. 在1978-79年担任刚果民主共和国金沙萨大学富布赖特教授之后,他的研究重点转移到金沙萨以及更广泛的撒哈拉以南非洲的生育率。 他还因在俄亥俄州立大学和宾州大学的教学而获得最高奖.

p56.original:
Daniel MacDonald, California State University, San Bernardino
    Professor Daniel MacDonald is the Chair of the Economics Department at California State University, San Bernardino. He earned his BA in mathematics and economics from Seton Hall University in 2007 and his economics PhD from the University of Massachusetts Amherst in 2013. Macdonald conducts economic research in labor economics, public policy (housing), and the economic history of the U.S. Consulting. He is also the author of the weekly Inland Empire Economic Update newsletter, which he started in 2021.
p56.zh: 加州州立大学丹尼尔·麦克唐纳,圣贝纳迪诺教授丹尼尔·麦克唐纳是加州州立大学圣贝纳迪诺分校经济学系主席.2007年他在塞顿霍尔大学获得数学和经济学学士学位,2013年在马萨诸塞阿姆赫斯特大学获得经济学博士学位.麦克多纳德在劳动经济学,公共政策(住房),以及美国经济史方面进行经济研究.咨询。 他也是他于2021年开始创办的"内陆帝国经济最新通讯"周刊的作者.

p57.original:
Steven A. Greenlaw, Professor Emeritus at University of Mary Washington
    Steven Greenlaw taught principles of economics for 39 years. In 1999, he received the Grellet C. Simpson Award for Excellence in Undergraduate Teaching at the University of Mary Washington. He is the author of Doing Economics: A Guide to Doing and Understanding Economic Research, as well as a variety of articles on economics pedagogy and instructional technology, published in the Journal of Economic Education, the International Review of Economic Education, and other outlets. He wrote the module on Quantitative Writing for Starting Point: Teaching and Learning Economics, the web portal on best practices in teaching economics. Steven Greenlaw lives in Alexandria, Virginia with his wife Kathy. Since retiring from full-time teaching, he has been doing faculty development work and other writing projects.
p57.zh: (原始内容存档于2018-09-26). Steven A.格林劳,玛丽·华盛顿大学荣誉教授史蒂文·格林劳教授教授经济学原理,为期39年.1999年,他获得了格列特C.辛普森奖 玛丽·华盛顿大学本科教学杰出奖. 他是《从事经济学:从事和理解经济研究指南》的作者,以及发表在《经济教育杂志》、《经济教育国际评论》等刊物上的各种关于经济学教学和教学技术的文章。 他撰写了"起点的量化写作:教学经济学"模块,即"教学经济学中的最佳做法"的网络门户. 史蒂文·格林劳与妻子凯西住在弗吉尼亚州的亚历山大. 自全职教师退休后,他一直在从事教研室发展和其他写作项目。

p62.original: Answers to Questions in the Book

p63.original: Students can find answers to Self-Checks in the Answer Key. Answers to all Review Questions, Critical Thinking Questions, and Problems are provided only to instructors in the Instructor Answer Guide via the Instructor Resources page.
p63.zh: 学生可以在回答键中找到自我检查的答案.对所有审查问题、批判性思考问题和问题的回答,仅通过教员资源网页在《教员回答指南》中提供给教员。

p66.original: We’ve compiled additional resources for both students and instructors, including Getting Started Guides, an instructor’s manual, test bank, and image slides. Instructor resources require a verified instructor account, which you can apply for when you log in or create your account on OpenStax.org. Take advantage of these resources to supplement your OpenStax book.
p66.zh: 我们为学生和教官汇编了额外资源,包括《开始指南》、教官手册、测试库和图像幻灯片。教官资源需要一个经过验证的教官账户,您可以在OpenStax.org登录或创建您的账户时申请该账户.利用这些资源来补充您的 OpenStax 书 。

p67.original: Premium Course Shells: These robust course cartridges are preloaded with assessments, activities, discussion prompts, readings, and other assignable material. They are logically organized to match the way you manage your course, with pre-lecture, synchronous, and post-lecture experiences. Activities and assessments are designed so that the answers are not easily found via online searches. These offerings are provided for D2L, Canvas, and Blackboard, and may require support from campus instructional technology or related teams to import and integrate.
p67.zh: Premium Course Shells:这些坚固的课程盒预装有评估,活动,讨论提示,读物,以及其他可分配的材料.它们的逻辑组织 与你的课程管理方式相匹配 与前课,同步课,后课的经验。活动和评估的设计是为了不易通过在线搜索找到答案。 这些供品是为D2L,Canvas,和Blackboard提供的,可能需要校园教学技术或相关团队的支持才能导入和整合.

p68.original: Enhanced Lecture PowerPoint Slides: These lecture slides include selected graphics from the text, key concepts and definitions, examples, and discussion questions.
p68.zh: 增强讲座PowerPoint幻灯片:这些讲座幻灯片包括文本中选定的图形,关键概念和定义,实例,以及讨论问题.

p69.original: Test Bank: The test bank contains multiple choice, short answer, and essay questions for each chapter of the textbook. Since many instructors use these questions in graded assignments, we ask that you not post these questions and the answers on any publicly available websites.
p69.zh: 测试库:测试库包含教科书各章的多个选择,简短的答案,以及散文问题. 由于许多教员在分级任务中使用这些问题,我们要求你们不要在任何公开网站上张贴这些问题和答案。

p70.original: Instructor Solution Guide: The instructor solutions guide contains the instructor-facing answers to the problems and exercises within the textbook.
p70.zh: 指导员解决方案指南:指导员解决方案指南包含指导员对问题和教科书中练习的解答.

p71.original: Video Guide: This video guide is a collection of videos recommended by instructors and grouped topically by OpenStax textbook chapters.
p71.zh: 视频指南:本视频指南是教官推荐的视频集,由OpenStax教科书章节按主题分组.

p72.original: Polling Questions: Spark discussion and support in-class learning and engagement using this set of polling questions. Survey students' understanding by a raise of hands or by pairing these questions with your polling technology; 3–4 questions are provided for each chapter.
p72.zh: 投票问题:用这组投票问题进行火花讨论和支持班内学习和接触. 通过举手或将这些问题与投票技术结合起来来调查学生的理解情况;每章都提供3-4个问题。

p74.original: Academic integrity builds trust, understanding, equity, and genuine learning. While students may encounter significant challenges in their courses and their lives, doing their own work and maintaining a high degree of authenticity will result in meaningful outcomes that will extend far beyond their college career. Faculty, administrators, resource providers, and students should work together to maintain a fair and positive experience.
p74.zh: 学术诚信建设了信任,理解,平等,以及真正的学习. 虽然学生在课程和生活中可能遇到重大挑战,但从事自己的工作并保持高度真实性将产生有意义的成果,远远超出他们的大学生涯。学院,行政人员,资源提供者,学生应当共同做好工作,保持公平,积极的经验.

p75.original: We realize that students benefit when academic integrity ground rules are established early in the course. To that end, OpenStax has created an interactive to aid with academic integrity discussions in your course.
p75.zh: 我们意识到,当课程早期确立学术诚信基本规则时,学生将受益。 为此,OpenStax创建了互动功能,帮助您在课程中进行学术诚信讨论.

p76.original: Visit our academic integrity slider. Click and drag icons along the continuum to align these practices with your institution and course policies. You may then include the graphic on your syllabus, present it in your first course meeting, or create a handout for students.
p76.zh: 参观我们的学术诚信滑板.点击和拖动图标沿连续体,使这些做法与你的机构和课程政策相一致。 然后,您可以将教学大纲中的图形,在第一次课程会议上介绍,或者为学生创造助益。

p77.original: At OpenStax we are also developing resources supporting authentic learning experiences and assessment. Please visit this book’s page for updates. For an in-depth review of academic integrity strategies, we highly recommend visiting the International Center of Academic Integrity (ICAI) website at https://academicintegrity.org/.
p77.zh: 在OpenStax,我们还开发资源,支持真正的学习经验和评估。 请访问此书的页面获取最新消息。 为了深入审查学术廉政战略,我们强烈建议访问国际学术廉政中心网站https://academicintegrity.org/。

p79.original: OpenStax partners with the Institute for the Study of Knowledge Management in Education (ISKME) to offer Community Hubs on OER Commons—a platform for instructors to share community-created resources that support OpenStax books, free of charge. Through our Community Hubs, instructors can upload their own materials or download resources to use in their own courses, including additional ancillaries, teaching material, multimedia, and relevant course content. We encourage instructors to join the hubs for the subjects most relevant to your teaching and research as an opportunity both to enrich your courses and to engage with other faculty. To reach the Community Hubs, visit www.oercommons.org/hubs/openstax.
p79.zh: OpenStax与教育知识管理研究所(ISKME)合作,在OER Commons上提供社区枢纽——一个教官分享社区创造的资源的平台,支持OpenStax图书免费. 通过我们的社区中心站,教员可以上传自己的材料或下载资源,用于自己的课程,包括额外的辅助课程、教材、多媒体和相关课程内容。 我们鼓励教员加入与你的教学和研究最相关的学科的中心,作为丰富课程和与其他教员接触的机会。 要联系社区中心,请访问www.oercommons.org/hubs/openstax。

p81.original: As allies in making high-quality learning materials accessible, our technology partners offer optional low-cost tools that are integrated with OpenStax books. To access the technology options for your text, visit your book page on OpenStax.org.
p81.zh: 作为提供高质量学习材料的盟国,我们的技术伙伴提供了可选的低成本工具,这些工具与OpenStax书籍相结合。 要访问您的文本的技术选项, 请访问 OpenStax.org 上的您的书页 。
